races.name: VIP Enhancement Packages At Southwell Racecourse Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Drish Samphire
runners_data.note: Has been off for 524 days and returns a 2-year-old with very limited form, finishing tailed off in recent runs; a genuine hold-up type who will race towards the rear, but the lengthy absence and consistent fading in the finish make it very hard to trust.|

runners_data.name: Highfield Jewel
runners_data.note: Sara Ender's yard is 1 from 4 in the last 14 days which is a mild positive, but this horse has only managed placed efforts at best and shows a hold-up tendency that will push it into traffic in a compressed sprint field.|

runners_data.name: Posh Maisie
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has a persistent tendency to fade in the closing stages, which is a significant concern in a sprint finish where the final burst is everything; naturally races from rear and is redistriubted forward on the map, meaning its true position will be further back.|

runners_data.name: Sir Benedict
runners_data.note: Veteran 8-year-old with two placed efforts in similar-going sprint races and a natural tendency to race from behind, though the pace map pushes him forward given the field makeup; Andrew Mullen is a strong handler of this type and may find a handier berth by default.|

runners_data.name: Top Star
runners_data.note: Tongue-tied and with two placed efforts from hold-up positions over similar going, this Dean Ivory runner will likely find itself further forward than ideal in a field with no genuine leader; J F Egan's experience may help him find the right spot.|

runners_data.name: Uncle Sam
runners_data.note: Has a win and three places from 15 similar-going runs, the best conversion rate in the field; off 191 days which is the key concern, but Tom Eaves is adept at placing horses in sprint finishes and this is a competitive OR-50 horse in a weak classified event.|

runners_data.name: Blueaway
runners_data.note: Consistent record of mid-pack finishes on standard going and a 7lb claimer in Harry Vigors on board; the horse races naturally from behind and is redistributed forward on the map, but form shows it has struggled to break into the frame without a strong pace to chase.|

runners_data.name: Havin A Flyer
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' yard is 1 from 18 in the past 14 days which dampens enthusiasm, but Havin A Flyer has placed twice from 10 similar-going runs and wears a tongue-tie; Clifford Lee gives this runner a quality pilot edge in a field where jockey skill matters greatly.|

runners_data.name: Bust A Moon
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (h) and has a deeply negative recent run string including two last-of-field finishes at Southwell; a natural hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield on the map masks an even further back expected racing position in reality.|

runners_data.name: Desert Champion
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has placed once from eight similar-going runs, but the form string of 88786 shows an uncomfortably consistent pattern of mid-pack finishes without progress; David Nolan is a class jockey who may coax more from this horse, but the fade flag is a concern.|

runners_data.name: Dottie Diamond
runners_data.note: Has placed fourth on her most recent start over 5f on standard going, which is her best recent effort; Finley Marsh is a claiming apprentice, and the horse races naturally from behind, though positional redistribution means she may find herself further forward than expected in this leaderless field.|

races.paceDynamic: Every runner in this 11-horse field carries a hold-up or come-from-behind profile, meaning there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse likely to set a genuine, controlled pace from the off. The result will almost certainly be a slow-burn, tactical crawl from the gates before the field bunches and explodes into a flat-out sprint over the final two furlongs — a shape that is notoriously difficult to read and heavily influenced by draw, bounce, and who quickens first. Uncle Sam and Havin A Flyer hold the highest OR ratings and the most relevant similar-going form, and in a sprint finish their ability to sustain a run from a mid-pack position becomes their primary weapon. This race shape — a compressed, late-burst sprint finish — favours horses who can produce a sharp, sustained late surge from a prominent enough position in the pack, meaning any runner who can travel handy off a slow gallop and then unleash a turn of foot has a significant edge over pure hold-up types who need cover and a genuine pace to aim at. The field holds more hold-up types than can all fulfil that role; Uncle Sam, Havin A Flyer, and Desert Champion are most likely to secure a workable position given their form and jockey quality.

watchPoints.text: Uncle Sam is 191 days off the track — watch the market move; if well-backed on return he becomes the form anchor in what is otherwise a very thin field.

With no genuine front-runner, watch for a false start or extreme tardy beginning from one of the redistributed hold-up types as all 11 attempt to slot in behind horses that don't exist — traffic chaos in the first furlong is a real risk.

Desert Champion wears a hood and has a fade flag — if he jumps well and finds himself at the front of a slow-moving pack, watch whether he compounds badly in the final furlong and blocks the run of trailing horses.
Havin A Flyer's trainer Rebecca Menzies is running at 1 from 18 over the last 14 days — monitor whether the market reflects this cold spell or fades the runner accordingly before the off.

Sir Benedict has placed twice in similar-going 5f sprints and is an 8-year-old who knows his job; watch his draw — a low-to-middle stall could allow Andrew Mullen to push forward into the leadership vacuum without burning any energy.

races.name: Ladies Day Sunday 16th August Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: J Street
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with place form on AW Standard (2nd, 3rd in her last five), but Southwell's straight 5f makes it structurally hard to make up ground; Billy Garritty is a course regular and 13 days since last run is a positive freshness angle, though her sim-going record is 0W3P from 14 opportunities.|

runners_data.name: La Belle Forest
runners_data.note: Won on AW Standard at Southwell over 5f and has followed up with a third on the same surface, giving her the strongest course-and-distance profile in the field; Edward Greatrex booking is notable for an Archie Watson 3yo, and 14 days since last run is routine preparation.|

runners_data.name: Life After Love
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with nine runs on similar going yielding three wins and four places — the most prolific sim-going profile in the race; 31-day absence is the key query, and her Prominent style tag carries a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 suggesting she may not fully replicate front-running dominance, but she remains the single biggest influence on how this race is run.|

runners_data.name: Torfrida
runners_data.note: 345 days off the track is the dominant concern and dwarfs all other factors here; a genuine hold-up type whose natural racing position has been absorbed into midfield on the map by the volume of similar horses in this field, and the Pam Sly yard have only one runner in the past five days, limiting confidence in race-fitness.|

runners_data.name: Startling
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has won over this exact 5f AW Standard trip and is trained by John Wainwright whose stable has fired in three winners from seven runs in the past 14 days; the pull-up (P) in recent form is a flag, but 13 days since last run and an apprentice claiming 5lbs brings the weight in line.|

runners_data.name: Solid Bond
runners_data.note: Headgear (t, tongue-tie) worn for the first time or continued use can sharpen focus at the break, which matters on a fast 5f; however, a true hold-up type whose natural role is towards the rear, placed into midfield here simply because the rear is overcrowded, and her last five runs show no finish better than 5th.|

runners_data.name: Fantasy Obsessor
runners_data.note: Back-to-back AW Standard 2nd-place finishes are her best credentials, and the headgear (p, cheekpieces) adds early pace to a natural hold-up profile; Michael Appleby's trainer 14-day strike rate is 0/22 which is a significant negative flag, and her true racing position is further back than where she is mapped on this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Sarafina Mshairi
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on AW Standard and has placed four times at the trip, giving her a solid surface profile; she steps back to 5f here where she was 9th last time on Good, and the 7lb claimer Harry Vigors (7) is a weight-saving positive, though the 31-day break on a first run for a lightly-resourced yard warrants caution.|

races.paceDynamic: Life After Love is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to her outside, she should stride clear from the gates and control tempo on Standard Fibresand at Southwell's sharp 5f. Startling and Sarafina Mshairi are the only other prominently-inclined runners and will slot in behind, meaning the pace is sustainable rather than pressured — a single-figure splits scenario rather than a true test. This setup strongly favours a horse who can either track the leader in second or third and pick up in the closing stages, or an on-pace type who handles the even gallop; genuine hold-up horses face a structurally difficult task on a straight 5f with limited late sectionals to exploit. This field carries more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate — Fantasy Obsessor, Torfrida, and Solid Bond are all true rear-of-field types redistributed to midfield on the map, and Life After Love with Startling are most likely to actually secure the prominent positions they want.

watchPoints.text: Life After Love's 31-day absence is the race's single biggest pivot — if she is ring-rusty breaking from the gates, the entire controlled-pace scenario unravels and the two tracking horses (Sarafina Mshairi, Startling) become immediate dangers.

Fantasy Obsessor, Torfrida, and Solid Bond are all natural hold-up horses compressed into midfield by field composition — watch for traffic issues and positional friction in the early stages as these runners are likely to find themselves in unfamiliar ground positions.

Torfrida's 345-day layoff is extreme in a fast 5f handicap on Fibresand; watch for any early behavioural signs (sweating, reluctance to load) that would confirm fitness concerns and effectively remove her from contention before the start.

Startling's pull-up (P) in her last-but-one run and subsequent 8th and 3rd need monitoring in the betting market — if the market contracts on her it suggests connections have found an explanation, if she drifts it likely reflects unresolved fitness doubt.

La Belle Forest has the strongest course-and-distance profile in the field (1W2P on AW Standard at Southwell 5f) — watch whether the market acknowledges this angle, as any drift for a horse with this surface record would be a useful pricing signal.

races.name: Lionel Henry James Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Manbearpig
runners_data.note: Consistently finishes fifth in handicaps and has failed to win or place at similar level on this surface; truly runs from the back and the absence of any genuine pace to chase makes its task harder, with 33 days off for Rebecca Menzies doing little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Dalamara
runners_data.note: Course winner on Southwell's Fibresand at 8f is the most relevant credential here, and Ben Haslam's runner has placed twice from seven starts on similar going — though stepping up to 1m4f for the first time is the key question; races from off the pace as its natural style.

runners_data.name: Echo Valley
runners_data.note: Has finished outside the top three in all five career starts including twice over 10f on standard going, and Tom Symonds saddles just one runner in the last 14 days; stripped to the bone in terms of form, the horse will settle deep and needs a truly troubled race for rivals to have any chance.

runners_data.name: Project Kinsman
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts from six Southwell starts over this exact trip give it course-and-distance credentials that stand out in this field, though the ⚠ fade flag suggests it finds little under pressure; Philip Kirby's stable is out of form over the past 14 days and the headgear note adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Mountbatten
runners_data.note: A two-year-old returning after 178 days for Sir Mark Prescott, a trainer famous for targeting horses precisely when they are ready — the yard has two winners from eight recent runners and this step up to 1m4f on debut at the distance for a lightly-raced youngster is worth watching carefully.

runners_data.name: Spirit Dreamer
runners_data.note: Best recent form in the race — a second over 1m4f at Goodwood — makes it the form pick on trip evidence, and Andrew Balding's yard is firing with nine winners from 62 in the last 14 days; Jason Watson takes the ride and the headgear flag suggests connections are trying to unlock more.

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners carrying a hold-up profile and zero confirmed front-runners in this 1m4f Southwell handicap, the race faces a structural vacuum at the head of affairs — nobody wants to make it. The early stages will almost certainly be pedestrian, with the field crawling through the first half of the race as every rider waits for a rival to commit. That slow-burn tempo will compress the field into a tight bunch and the race will be decided in a short, sharp sprint over the final two furlongs, turning it effectively into a stamina-plus-turn-of-foot contest rather than a true test of staying ability. All six horses are classified as hold-up types, meaning no runner has a natural tactical advantage and the shape is genuinely open — Dalamara has winning form at this track on standard Fibresand and carries the most relevant course form, while Spirit Dreamer's second at Goodwood over 1m4f shows the best recent form-book evidence of handling this trip. This shape most favours horses with a sharp late sprint and positive course-and-distance form, as the winner will be the one who can quicken off a slow pace in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Mountbatten is trained by Sir Mark Prescott, who places horses with surgical precision — a 178-day break followed by a step up in trip on a surface he has not tried is a classic Prescott setup, and the stable's recent form (2/8 T14) demands attention.

Dalamara is the only runner with a winning strike on Southwell's standard Fibresand surface, and Ben Haslam's runner is 14 days fresh — course form is the most reliable edge in an otherwise formless field.

With no front-runner present, watch the early pace — if the field truly crawls for the first mile, positioning in the home straight will be chaotic and the horse that gets a clean rail run is at a premium.

Project Kinsman's ⚠ fade flag combined with a hold-up style in a race with no pace to chase is a significant tactical red flag — if the race produces a sprint finish, its tendency to find little late is a serious concern for backers.

Spirit Dreamer's headgear note suggests Andrew Balding is trying to sharpen its response, and a horse that has already run over the trip competitively at Goodwood is better equipped than most in this field if the race is truly run on class.

races.name: Southwell Racecourse Conferences And Events Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Monday 31st August Family Fun Day Confined Handicap (No Win Since The 2025 Flat Turf Season)

runners_data.name: Star Of Mali
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has won over this exact 7f Southwell trip in good recent form (won last time at this course and distance), perfectly suited to tracking the leader and striking in the final two furlongs; James Tate yard is 0/8 in the 14-day window but the horse's own course record here is a significant positive.

runners_data.name: Ribenska
runners_data.note: Unknown style tag leaves her positioning uncertain, but her one win on this going was over 7f at Southwell and she handles the surface well; Clifford Lee is a competent AW jockey and 43 days between runs is not a concern, though her form has been in and out (1-7-7 last three) which limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Albion
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose similar-going record at Southwell is a thin 2-from-9 with zero wins, and all her recent form has been on Good or Softer turf, making this all-weather Standard surface a question mark; the hood (headgear) is noted but she maps to the rear naturally and will need a strong pace to deliver her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Blazing Son
runners_data.note: Veteran 8-year-old who is a genuine hold-up performer by nature, pushed into the midfield map because the rear of the field is oversubscribed; his best recent effort here was a second over 7f on Standard and he handles the surface, but racing closer than he'd like blunts the effectiveness of his usual late challenge — discount accordingly.

runners_data.name: Silver Trumpet
runners_data.note: Carries the headgear flag (p) and is a hold-up type whose trainer Eve Johnson Houghton is in form at 5/28 over the past 14 days; her Southwell form is moderate (0 wins, 2 places from 7 runs on similar going) and she will need the pace to collapse ahead of her to get involved.

runners_data.name: Alfa Whiteburd
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) and a form string of 8-6-7-9-13 over 5-6f on varying ground raises genuine doubts about whether she can sustain the lead over 7f; Ivan Furtado has one winner from 26 over 14 days and this trip is a stretch — her role is pace-setter rather than winner.

runners_data.name: Reds And Wolves
runners_data.note: Three-year-old resuming after 384 days off the track with an unknown style profile — the 'U' tag and the long absence make her deeply unpredictable; all three runs were in 2024 and produced three mid-table finishes, so she would need a dramatic improvement to factor, though a fresh horse on Standard ground is never entirely ignorable.

runners_data.name: Judicature
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up runner whose true position at the back is unavailable in this field configuration, so she will race closer than suits; her best recent run was a second over 7f on Soft for a different trainer, and Joel Parkinson & Sue Smith are 0/8 in the 14-day window — the style mismatch is a real handicap here.

runners_data.name: Cy Twombly
runners_data.note: Consistent bottom-of-the-handicap performer (OR 62) who races with a tongue-tie (tp) and whose six Southwell runs on Standard have produced zero wins; a genuine hold-up type placed into midfield by necessity, meaning he will neither get his natural position nor benefit from sitting on the pace — tough ask at this level.

runners_data.name: Macanudo
runners_data.note: Returning from a 426-day absence for Ian Williams (0/27 in 14 days), this 3-year-old's form reads as a string of mid-division finishes on Standard at Southwell — workmanlike rather than exciting; his natural style is hold-up but he too is squeezed into the midfield map, and a horse this far past its last run with no obvious angle is a significant each-way risk.

runners_data.name: Brunel Nation
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner, so no tactical assessment is relevant — connections should be noted for future entries as Richard Hughes has been 5/24 in the 14-day trainer window.

races.paceDynamic: Alfa Whiteburd is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 7f Southwell handicap and, with no serious challenger for the lead, David Nolan should be able to dictate at a measured, controlled gallop on Standard ground. That lone-leader scenario sets up a truly run but not pressured race — a sustainable tempo rather than a truly searching one, which keeps the front end competitive deep into the straight. Star Of Mali and Ribenska are the natural prominent players who will look to sit just behind Alfa Whiteburd and are best placed to capitalise if the pace is honest; the hold-up battalion — Blazing Son, Judicature, Cy Twombly and Macanudo — have been redistributed to midfield on the map precisely because the field houses more rear-track types than the race shape can accommodate, meaning several of them will race closer than ideal without securing their true position. The overall shape — one measured leader, a cluster of prominent/mid-division horses — strongly favours a prominent racer who tracks the gallop and pounces in the final two furlongs, as genuine closers will lack the sectional injection needed to reel in a controlled front-runner on this circuit.

watchPoints.text: Alfa Whiteburd (front-runner) has a style-fit flag and career form suggesting she is fragile over 7f — watch whether David Nolan can control the tempo or whether the field begins to mass-pressurise her approaching the home turn.

Blazing Son and Judicature are both genuine rear-track types forced into midfield by the congested field shape — if they are bumped or checked trying to find a lane in the straight, their already-discounted chances will evaporate entirely.

Reds And Wolves returns after 384 days and Macanudo after 426 days — watch the market moves for either of these; a significant plunge would suggest connections have strong home work and they should be tracked in-running even without obvious form.

Star Of Mali's 150-day absence is the one flag on what looks a solid candidate — watch whether Jason Watson settles him promptly out of the stalls and whether he travels with his usual fluency, as a rusty comeback could see him slightly short of peak sharpness at a crucial moment.

runners_data.name: Material Girl
runners_data.note: Produced a forward-placed run on Good ground last time but is a genuine hold-up type by profile; bumped into the surplus of closers in this mapping and will need everything to fall perfectly from a position she doesn't naturally want.

runners_data.name: Mimime
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby runner with a quiet 14-day strike rate (0/17) and a hold-up style; ran seventh on Good ground at 6f last time and needs a stronger gallop than Planet Seeker is likely to generate to deliver her best.

runners_data.name: Name The Day
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unexposed filly for Eve Johnson Houghton, who has a healthy 14-day strike rate (5/35); style listed as unknown so tactical flexibility is plausible, and 17 days since her last run is a workable freshen-up.

runners_data.name: Park Lane Penny
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado filly whose recent form reads 6th and 9th, both on Good ground but stepping back from 7f and 8f, so the return to 6f on Standard AW is an unknown quantity that is hard to upgrade on.

runners_data.name: Star Trail
runners_data.note: Debutant for D K Weld shipped from Ireland, completely unexposed on any surface; going is unknown and the absence of any form data makes her a genuine wildcard who could slot anywhere in the field.

runners_data.name: Star Velocity
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett newcomer with no racecourse experience and going unknown; the powerful trainer has form bringing debutants to win at lower tracks, but the absence of any public trial data demands caution.

runners_data.name: Town Queen
runners_data.note: K R Burke filly with a tidy three-race form string of consecutive runner-up finishes (all on Good ground, over 6-7f); prominent style suits this race shape well and Clifford Lee is experienced at Southwell.

runners_data.name: Veil Of Clouds
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford filly who ran fifth on Good ground at 6f last time; hold-up style means she needs some traffic to clear and a stronger gallop than the pace map suggests, but the yard fires at a reasonable rate.

runners_data.name: Planet Seeker
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's front-runner returns after 279 days off for what looks like the most significant absence in the field; won at 6f on Good and placed at Southwell previously, but fitness after that layoff is the central question, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that dictating here may be harder than it appears on paper.

runners_data.name: Gardening
runners_data.note: Lawrence Mullaney yard with a flat 14-day record (0/4); went 5th at 6f on Standard going last time suggesting some course-condition applicability (sim-going record 1 win from 2 runs), but holds-up naturally and has been pushed forward in the mapping — the true closing style may not find the late surge this pace map generates.

runners_data.name: Mass For Kathleen
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado filly who finished 3rd at 7f on Soft and 10th at 7f on Good; her natural desire to come from off the pace sits at odds with the race shape Planet Seeker is set to create, and the step back to 6f on Standard AW asks fresh questions.

races.paceDynamic: Planet Seeker is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with a long 279-day absence factored in, is likely to roll forward and control the fractions on a flat Southwell 6f without any natural challenger for the lead — Town Queen will attempt to press from a prominent position but lacks the natural pace to seriously disrupt. The resulting tempo is likely to be honest but not truly searching, with Planet Seeker setting a sustainable gallop that keeps the field strung out rather than compressed into a bunched finish. This shape most clearly favours horses who can travel prominently in the slipstream of the leader, respond when asked turning in, and sustain their effort to the line — a prominent-to-midfield profile wins here. Note that the field contains more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Material Girl, Gardening, and Mass For Kathleen are true closers who have been mapped to midfield, but Town Queen and Planet Seeker are the horses most likely to actually hold the prominent positions from the outset.

scenarios.trigger: If Planet Seeker's long absence (279 days) tells and the horse fades sharply from the 2f pole, gifting the race to a fresh legs finisher.
scenarios.body: If Planet Seeker's long absence (279 days) tells and the horse fades sharply from the 2f pole, gifting the race to a fresh legs finisher.

watchPoints.text: Watch Planet Seeker's early market moves — if significant support dries up close to post, the 279-day absence may be more of a concern than the odds reflect, reshaping the entire pace scenario.

Town Queen is the only horse likely to apply any pressure to Planet Seeker; if she misses the break or is outpaced early, the lead becomes completely uncontested and the race turns into a one-dimensional procession.

Star Trail and Star Velocity are both first-time starters with unknown going profiles — either could show natural pace or act as a traffic hazard mid-race, and their uncharted tactical styles make them factors in any scenario modelling.

Material Girl, Gardening, and Mass For Kathleen are all mapped forward of their natural position; watch at the start to see whether any of them are restrained back to their true hold-up spots, which would further isolate the genuine closers at the rear.

The entire field is fillies at novice level — watch the market for any unexposed runner (particularly Star Velocity for Ralph Beckett) showing significant late market moves, as debutants from major yards often carry unannounced ability at this level.

races.name: Golf And Gallop Southwell Golf Club Handicap

runners_data.name: Gaurdman
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Roger Varian two-year-old returning from a 265-day absence on debut turf form — the lengthy layoff for a young horse is the primary concern, though the prominent style suits the likely race shape if match-fit.|

runners_data.name: Enricher
runners_data.note: William Muir and Chris Grassick have this hold-up type in cracking heart having won on Standard recently (1/6f/STA), and the 24-day gap is comfortable — needs a testing pace to bring his late run into play on this straight track.|

runners_data.name: Ay Up Duck
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's horse has smart Southwell form at this trip but is a genuine pace horse whose natural position at the front is unavailable in this field — forced to race off its preferred style, which tempers its winning chance meaningfully.|

runners_data.name: Ghisa
runners_data.note: Two wins on Standard-going turf (1/7f/STA, 1/6f/STA) make this Charlie Fellowes three-year-old course-and-conditions savvy; the headgear (h) and 139-day absence are small flags but prominent style fits perfectly into the available second-on slot.|

runners_data.name: Blue Orbit
runners_data.note: Has one notable Standard-going placing (2/5f/STA) but the overall record of 0 wins from 8 career runs and a single place from 8 recent efforts is thin — a hold-up type who needs the race to develop favourably and the pace to genuinely lift.|

runners_data.name: Up The Agenda
runners_data.note: Jack Morland's horse carries a tremendous Southwell record (3W at STA, 4 places from 10 runs) and is a genuine pace horse, but that prominent position is already occupied — racing against its nature here is a real cost to its winning prospects.|

runners_data.name: Lady Kodiac
runners_data.note: James Tate's filly has two Standard-going wins (1/6f/STA, 1/6f/STA) and has a 19-day turnaround that keeps her sharp; as the lone confirmed front runner she holds the clearest tactical position in the field, though the STYLE_FIT flag cautions she may be operating at her ceiling at OR 85.|

runners_data.name: Sanaam
runners_data.note: Simon and Ed Crisford's hold-up horse won on Standard over 7f (1/7f/STA) and was placed over 6f at Goodwood — the headgear (p) is noted and the 13-day quick return for a yard hitting 5/22 in 14 days deserves respect, though the style demands a proper pace.|

runners_data.name: Bone Marra
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster runner with back-to-back Southwell victories (1/6f/STA, 2/6f/STA in recent hist) and a tongue tie flag — the proximity to the pace from a prominent position is ideally suited to the predicted race shape, and the trainer's 3/25 14-day strike rate is encouraging.|

races.paceDynamic: Lady Kodiac is the one confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to press her from the outside, she should be able to control the tempo from the gates on this straight 6f Southwell track under Jason Watson. Behind her, Ghisa and Bone Marra will look to slot in prominent positions, while Sanaam and Blue Orbit are the truest hold-up types who will need the race to develop in their favour. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate — Ay Up Duck and Up The Agenda are natural pace horses who will struggle to secure their preferred berths, and Lady Kodiac and Ghisa are most likely to actually claim the positions closest to the rail and the lead. A controlled, sustainable single-file pace set by Lady Kodiac shapes this as a race where prominence is a clear asset — horses who can travel in the first three or four without over-racing hold a material tactical advantage, and true deep closers face the additional burden of manufacturing their run on a track that rarely rewards those who give too much ground away early.

watchPoints.text: Lady Kodiac's ability to hold the front unchallenged is the pivotal factor — if she gets a soft lead from Watson, the entire race shape is decided from the first furlong; watch her draw position and early reaction from the stalls.

Ay Up Duck and Up The Agenda are natural pace horses who cannot get their preferred ground — if they force their way forward aggressively from the gates they could pressure Lady Kodiac and fundamentally change the race tempo beyond what the map projects.

Ghisa has not run for 139 days and carries headgear — watch for any signs of greenness or ring-rustiness in the pre-race market; if fit, the Standard-going course form is compelling, but the absence is a genuine concern.

Sanaam had a quick 13-day turnaround from a Crisford yard running at a 5/22 14-day strike rate — if the stable is targeting this race specifically, the hold-up horse's Standard form (1/7f/STA) could be sharper than it appears on paper.

Enricher's sole win came on Standard going at 6f and William Muir and Chris Grassick are working with just a 1/13 14-day strike — straightforward market drift would confirm whether the yard considers it live or a race-sharpener.|
